# Susumārajātaka (Ja 208)

**ID:** Ja 208
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Susumārajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Crocodile
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja208
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Susumārajātaka* (Ja 208) is a birth story set at Jetavana, delivered by the Buddha concerning Devadatta's attempts to murder him [SuttaCentral]. The Buddha relates that in a previous existence Devadatta similarly attempted to kill him, yet failed even to make him afraid [SuttaCentral]. In the story of the past, a crocodile's wife develops a craving for the heart of a monkey; the crocodile entices the monkey in an effort to kill him, but the monkey outwits the crocodile by claiming that monkeys do not carry their hearts inside their bodies, having hung his heart on a tree by the riverbank [Winternitz 1933]. Maurice Winternitz notes the humorous character of the fable and its close affinity to versions found in the *Pañcatantra* and in *Jātaka* 57 [Winternitz 1933]. In V. Fausböll's edition of the Jātaka commentary, it appears as the eighth text of its chapter [Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral records a full parallel to this narrative in the Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit *Mahāvastu* (Mvu 58, *The Jātaka of the Monkey*), which preserves the episode of the crocodile's wife demanding the heart of the monkey friend [SuttaCentral; Jones 1952]. Automated text-reuse searches by DharmaNexus detected no Pali-internal reuse nor any cross-language textual alignments with a score of 10 or above [DharmaNexus].
